# Gemma12B-RISCV

**An autonomous coding test generated by Qwen-Flash-Next, not a validated inference accelerator.**

This repository preserves an experiment in having **Qwen-Flash-Next autonomously generate** a RISC-V-controlled accelerator exploration: architecture notes, analytical sizing models, SystemVerilog RTL, Python numerical references, and simulation harnesses. It is published to inspect what the model produced, including its limitations, rather than to present it as a human-designed or production-ready chip.

The autonomous-generation attribution is supplied by the project owner. Publication preparation includes documentation cleanup and rerunning the available checks; that does not establish independent correctness of the whole design or the generated research. No complete generation transcript or exact model checkpoint/quantization is included, so this is not a reproducible benchmark of Qwen-Flash-Next itself.

The current sizing target is **Gemma 4 12B Unified**, initially its text decoder. An older Gemma 3 estimate is retained separately. Gemma is the workload being explored; Qwen-Flash-Next is the model that generated the experiment.

## What exists

| Component | Implemented scope | Important limit |
|---|---|---|
| [RISC-V core](rtl/rv32i_core.sv) | RV32I, Zicsr, Zifencei, machine-mode traps/CSRs, hardware handling of misaligned scalar accesses | No U/S modes, PMP, interrupt sources, or Sdtrig |
| Control-side vector instructions | RVV 1.0 subset: VLEN=128, ELEN=32, LMUL=1, unmasked SEW 8/16/32; configuration, unit-stride memory, selected arithmetic and reductions | Element-serial implementation; **not full RVV and not RVV-compliant** |
| [Q4 dot unit](rtl/q4_dot_product.sv) | 32 signed Q4 × INT8 lanes with INT32 result | Not a complete model inference kernel |
| [Streaming Q4 GEMV tile](rtl/q4_gemv_tile.sv) | Packed Q4 groups, resident INT8 activations, signed Q16.16 group scales, 64-bit fixed-point accumulation | Not the proposed BF16/FP32 datapath; no DMA or external-memory controller |
| [Python Q4 reference](sw/q4_gemv.py) | Signed-nibble packing, per-group scaling and GEMV | Python floating-point reference, not a bit-exact floating-point hardware oracle |
| [Gemma sizing model](model/gemma4.py) | Weight/KV capacity, decode rooflines, chunked-prefill and concurrency estimates | Analytical bounds, **not measured inference performance** |

There is no end-to-end Gemma inference implementation, model-quality evaluation, demonstrated FPGA deployment, fabricated chip, or measured silicon throughput/power in this repository. Passing simulation cases does not prove that arbitrary programs or full models work.

## Run the Python examples

Python 3.10 or newer; standard library only. No model download is required.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/PyroFlareX/Gemma12B-RISCV.git
cd Gemma12B-RISCV

python3 model/gemma4.py
python3 sw/q4_gemv.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s model -p 'test_*.py' -v
python3 -m unittest discover -s sw -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

`model/gemma4.py` prints estimated capacity and throughput/latency ceilings for assumed bandwidth, compute, context, and batch sizes. It does not run Gemma. The Q4 example prints `[-2.75]` for its small synthetic input.

## RTL simulation and recorded results

The following checks were rerun during publication preparation on 2026-10-19 (UTC), using the commands and dependency revisions below.

| Check | Observed result | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Python sizing and Q4 reference checks | 6 sizing tests and 3 Q4 tests passed; both example programs ran | Numerical boundaries, packing, row/group scaling |
| [RTL regression](sw/regress.sh) | 63 suites: 61 passes, 2 expected failures, zero unexpected failures | Hand-written core bench, two Q4 tile configurations, two vector cases, and upstream scalar/privileged tests |
| Upstream `riscv-tests` within that regression | rv32ui 42/42; rv32mi 14/16 | Expected failures: `breakpoint` (Sdtrig) and `pmpaddr` (PMP), neither implemented |
| [ACT/Sail signature comparison](sw/act_regress.sh) | 39/39 `rv32i/I` cases passed | Same ELF executed by Sail and RTL; signature-region comparison, not just a success marker |

These are limited simulation results, not RISC-V certification or full vector compliance. The ACT runner does not cover vector, privileged, or other extension groups.

### Toolchain

The shell runners require Bash, Python, Icarus Verilog (`iverilog`, `vvp`), GNU coreutils (including `timeout`), `grep`, `awk`, and a bare-metal `riscv64-unknown-elf` GCC/binutils toolchain with RV32 vector assembly support. GCC 13.2.0, Icarus 12.0, and Sail 0.15 were available for publication verification.

External test sources are not bundled. The existing runners use these upstream checkouts:

- [`riscv-tests`](https://github.com/riscv-software-src/riscv-tests), revision `d7e86f701b929b5d801f8cda1a4871ab05f452bb`, with its `env/` submodule at `6de71edb142be36319e380ce782c3d1830c65d68`.
- [`riscv-arch-test`](https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-arch-test), revision `960a780a59e9bce132184bcc8124a9a3c2ca011c`, including `rtl-test/` configuration and linker files.
- [Sail RISC-V simulator](https://github.com/riscv/sail-riscv), version 0.15.

After obtaining those prerequisites, run from this repository root, substituting your checkout and binary paths:

```sh
RISCV_TESTS=/path/to/riscv-tests bash sw/regress.sh
ACT=/path/to/riscv-arch-test SAIL=/path/to/sail_riscv_sim bash sw/act_regress.sh
```

`RVGCC_DIR` can point to the directory containing the cross-toolchain binaries. `IVERILOG` and `VVP` override simulator paths; `IVL_B` supplies an extracted Icarus backend directory. `OUT` overrides each runner's temporary output directory. The defaults are `/tmp/rv-regress` and `/tmp/rv-act`; use distinct `OUT` directories for concurrent runs.

## Verification limits

The Python examples, both Python test groups, shell syntax checks, RTL regression, and ACT/Sail comparison were exercised for publication. These checks do not independently validate the generated architecture, cited model specifications, marketplace listings, full instruction-set semantics, or end-to-end model quality. No RTL functionality was changed during publication cleanup.

## Design notes and caveats

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): generated model assumptions, compute/memory partition, and ideal performance ceilings.
- [Memory](docs/memory.md): generated memory-sizing arithmetic and historical marketplace observations, **not verified procurement advice or a bill of materials**.
- [Archived Gemma 3 estimate](model/gemma12b.py): unverified historical configuration, not the current sizing input.

Peak GDDR bandwidth is not sustained throughput. The roofline omits real controller/PHY behavior, implementation efficiency, and parts of the model. Q4 accuracy, complete prefill/GEMM kernels, DMA, memory controllers, synthesis/timing closure, physical design, and board power remain unvalidated. Qwen-inspired draft/speculative features are proposals, not implemented hardware capabilities.
